paragraphs.source_en: “So, as I was just saying, the other side says they do not care about money or property, but would like the man himself to have some qualification attached to him. By qualification, to put it simply, I mean a title. If he became a doctor, they would give him their daughter, they insist... no, no, they are not insisting; you must not misunderstand me. The other day, when Mrs. Kaneda came, Meitei was there and kept saying all sorts of ridiculous things to interfere. Of course, this was not your fault. Mrs. Kaneda even praised you, saying you were free of flattery and a very honest, good man. It was entirely Meitei’s fault. So, you see, they say that if the man became a doctor, then they too could hold their heads high before society and preserve their dignity. What do you think? Could Mr. Mizushima possibly submit a doctoral dissertation soon and receive the degree of doctor? No, really, if it were only Kaneda, he would not care a straw about doctors or bachelors, but one has to consider society, you know; such matters cannot be handled quite so simply.”

paragraphs.source_en: “Well, well, what a rare guest.
